categories.howToSpot: Look for any combination of cards whose values add to 15. A ten-value card pairs with a five, while smaller cards can make several combinations.
Two cards of the same rank score a pair. Three of a rank makes three pairs, and four makes six pairs.
Three or more consecutive ranks score a run. Duplicate ranks can multiply the run through pairs.
Four cards of one suit score a hand flush. A fifth card, the cut, can extend it when it matches too.
A jack in the hand can become his nobs when the cut matches its suit. It is easy to miss because the cut decides it.

primer.body: Cribbage is a race to 121 points. You score by making combinations in your hand and crib, then by playing cards in order during pegging. The first player to reach the finish wins.
primer.tip: A fifteen is any combination of cards totaling 15, worth 2 points.
primer.title: The goal

primer.body: Use a standard 52-card deck. Aces are low and count as 1. Number cards keep their values, while jacks, queens, and kings count as 10 for fifteens.
primer.title: Meet the deck

primer.body: Each player receives six cards and discards two to the dealer's crib. The non-dealer cuts the starter card, which joins both hands and the crib for scoring.
primer.tip: The dealer wants a strong crib. The pone tries to starve it.
primer.title: Deal and discard

primer.body: Score every combination of 15, then pairs, runs, and flushes. Add one for his nobs when a jack matches the starter's suit. The same starter card can create several bonuses at once.
primer.tip: Count in the same order every time so your points do not disappear.
primer.title: Count the hand

primer.body: After the starter is cut, players alternate playing one card while keeping the running total at or below 31. Score for 15, pairs, runs, 31, go, and the last card.
primer.tip: Say the running total out loud. It is the center of every pegging decision.
primer.title: Peg the cards

primer.body: That is the whole loop: choose a discard, peg carefully, count every combination, and keep an eye on the board. The drills teach each skill one room at a time, five minutes at a stretch.
primer.title: You are ready

items.backBody: Cribbage uses a standard 52-card deck. Each player is dealt six cards, discards two to the crib, and then the starter card is cut from the deck.
items.frontSubtitle: Start with the shape of the game

items.backBody: Clubs, diamonds, hearts, and spades each have thirteen ranks. Suit matters for flushes and his nobs. Most fifteens, pairs, and runs care about rank or value instead.
Aces count as 1. Number cards keep their number. Jacks, queens, and kings each count as 10. The rank still matters for pairs and runs.
Every distinct combination totaling 15 scores 2 points. A hand can contain several fifteens, and each one is counted separately.
Two cards with the same rank score 2 points. Three of a kind contains three separate pairs, and four of a kind contains six.
Three consecutive ranks score 3 points, four score 4, and so on. Suits may be mixed. Duplicate ranks can create double, double-double, or triple runs.

After the discard, the non-dealer cuts the deck and the starter card joins both hands and the crib. It can create new fifteens, pairs, runs, a flush, or his nobs. A jack as the starter also pegs 2 for the dealer, called his heels.
If your hand contains a jack that matches the starter card's suit, score one point for his nobs. The jack does not need to match the starter's rank.
Both players discard two cards to the dealer's crib. The dealer counts the crib after counting their own hand, so dealer discards are both an opportunity and a risk.
Players move pegs along a board with 120 holes plus a final game hole. The first player to reach 121 wins, so a safe point now can matter more than a perfect-looking hand later.

6-7-8-9-10 is a five-card run worth 5, regardless of the mixed suits. It also hides two fifteens, 6 with 9 and 7 with 8, for a full count of 9.
Four 2s contain six separate pairs for 12. The 2s and the 10 reach 12, 14, 16, and 18 but never fifteen, so the duplicate rank is the entire count.
The 5 makes fifteen with the 10 and again with the jack, for 4 points. Nothing repeats a rank, and 4-5 never reaches a third consecutive card.
Two 3s and two 4s let 3-4-5 form four different ways, 12 points of runs. Add 4 for the two pairs and 4 for the two fifteens and the hand counts 20.
Ace through 5 is a five-card run for 5 points, and the five cards together total exactly fifteen for 2 more. Aces are low, so the run starts at the ace.

items.explanation: Muggins is an optional rule. When players agree to use it (the American Cribbage Congress calls it the only optional rule and requires it to be announced before play), an opponent can claim points you failed to peg during play or to count in your hand or crib. Without it, missed points are simply lost.

items.explanation: A duplicate rank gives the consecutive sequence two ways to be formed, doubling the run's points.

items.explanation: Aces are low in cribbage, so A-2-3 is a run. The ace does not wrap around from king.
